title: How Long Does Hardwood Floor Refinishing Take? Day-by-Day Timeline for Lynnwood Homes
meta: Hardwood floor refinishing takes 3 to 4 days for a natural finish, 4 to 5 with stain and 1 for a recoat. Wills Flooring's day-by-day timeline for Lynnwood.
keywords: how long does hardwood floor refinishing take, hardwood floor refinishing timeline, how many days to refinish hardwood floors, refinishing floors day by day, Lynnwood WA floor refinishing, when can I walk on refinished floors

blocks.lead: Refinishing a typical Lynnwood main floor takes 3 to 4 working days for a natural finish, 4 to 5 days with stain, and a single day for a screen-and-recoat.
blocks.detail: Add 24 hours before you walk on it in socks, 72 hours before furniture goes back, and about two weeks before rugs and full cure. The size of the floor matters less than you think; the number of coats and their dry times set the schedule.

blocks.html: The question behind this question is usually "how long do we have to live somewhere else?" In Lynnwood that often means a family in an Alderwood or Martha Lake rambler that just pulled up 40-year-old carpet, found oak underneath and now needs to know whether to book a hotel, stay with family in Everett or camp in the bedrooms. Here is exactly what happens each day on a Wills Flooring refinish, and what stretches or shortens it.

blocks.text: Day by day: a natural sand and refinish

items.text: We measure, check wood thickness and moisture, and give you a firm price. You clear the rooms. If carpet is still down, we pull it, pad and staples the morning we start.
items.note: Ramblers with oak under carpet: add half a day for tear-out

items.text: Vacuum-connected drum and edge sanders take the floor to bare wood in two or three grit passes. Old finish, gray boards and most stains disappear today. Loudest day; most people go to work and come home to a raw floor.
Board repairs, filling of nail holes and gaps, final buff, then the first coat of Bona sealer. From this point the floor is off limits to everyone, including pets.
items.note: Stain jobs: stain goes on today instead and dries overnight

items.text: Light abrasion between coats, vacuum, tack and the second coat of water-based finish. Water-based Bona dries in 2 to 3 hours, which is why we can finish in days, not weeks.
Third coat goes on in the morning. Socks-only walking is fine after 24 hours. Furniture with felt pads after 72 hours. Rugs, rolling chairs and wet mopping wait two weeks.

blocks.text: Can you live in the house while it happens?

items.title: Refinishing one floor of a two-story or split-level
items.text: Usually yes. Bedrooms upstairs stay usable, and you route around the work through a garage or back door. Many Alderwood split-levels work this way. The kitchen is the hard part if it is part of the job.

items.title: Refinishing a whole single-level rambler
items.text: Plan to be out from the sealer coat on day 2 until the final coat has 24 hours on it. That is three nights for natural, four for stain. Most Lynnwood families stay with relatives or book a hotel by the mall.

items.title: Pets and kids
items.text: Off the floor from day 2 until 24 hours after the final coat, no exceptions. Paw prints in a fresh coat are the most common callback we see, and they mean a re-sand of that area.

items.title: Smell and dust
items.text: Bona water-based finish has low odor and is dry to the touch in hours. Our sanders are vacuum-connected; the $250 containment option seals doorways and runs an air scrubber for occupied homes.

items.title: Martha Lake rambler, 850 sq ft
items.text: Oak under carpet, natural finish, no stairs. Carpet out Monday morning, sanded by Monday night, final coat Wednesday. Furniture back Saturday.

items.title: Alderwood split-level, 950 sq ft + 13 stairs
items.text: Stained a light natural-oak tone. Stairs sanded with the floor. Stain Tuesday, coats Wednesday through Friday. Back on it in socks Saturday.

items.title: Meadowdale townhome, 600 sq ft
items.text: Ten-year-old finish, dull but intact. Screen and recoat, in at 8 a.m. and out by 3 p.m. Furniture back Wednesday evening.

blocks.title: The Lynnwood scheduling reality:
blocks.text: Because the work sits ten minutes from our showroom on 196th, we can often start Lynnwood jobs on short notice in fall and winter. Summer is different; May through September books three to five weeks out. If you are planning around a move or new carpet upstairs, call early and lock the dates.

items.html: Rooms not cleared when we arrive. Every hour spent moving furniture is an hour not sanding, and it can push the final coat to the next day.
Unfixed leaks. A floor with a dishwasher or window leak must dry to normal moisture before sanding, or it will cup after finishing. We test on day 1 and will not sand wet wood.
Picking stain color on the day. Choose from samples at the estimate. We can test two colors on your floor on day 2, but a third or fourth means the stain slips a day.
Moving furniture back early. Water-based finish feels dry at 24 hours but is soft for about a week. Dragging a couch across it on day 2 leaves marks that only another coat fixes.

Not checking for a recoat option. If the finish is only dull, a one-day recoat at $1.99 per sq ft beats a four-day sanding at $3.99. Our refinish or recoat guide explains how to tell, and the refinishing page lists what every job includes.

faq.q: How long does it take to refinish 1,000 sq ft of hardwood floors?
faq.a: Three to four working days for a natural finish, four to five with stain. Size has less effect than people expect because each coat needs the same dry time regardless of area. A screen-and-recoat on the same 1,000 sq ft is done in a single day.

faq.q: How long after refinishing can you walk on hardwood floors?
faq.a: With Bona water-based finish, walk in socks after 24 hours, wear shoes and put furniture back with felt pads after 72 hours, and wait about two weeks before laying rugs, rolling chairs across it or wet mopping. Oil-based finishes take roughly twice as long at each stage.

faq.q: Do I have to move out while my floors are refinished?
faq.a: For a whole single-level home, plan to be out from the first coat on day 2 until 24 hours after the last coat, usually three nights. For a two-story or split-level where only one level is being done, most Lynnwood families stay and route around the work.

faq.q: Why does stain add a full day?
faq.a: Stain has to dry completely, normally overnight, before the first clear coat can go on top, or the finish will not bond and can peel. Dark stains and cold, damp days can stretch that to two nights. Everything after the stain follows the normal coat schedule.

faq.q: Can floors be refinished in winter in Lynnwood?
faq.a: Yes. We refinish year-round. Water-based finish cures slower in a cold, damp house, so we keep the heat on and run air movers between coats, which usually holds the standard three to four day timeline. Winter also has much better availability than summer.

faq.q: How long does a screen and recoat take?
faq.a: One day. The floor is abraded lightly, vacuumed, and given one fresh coat of finish, typically in six to eight hours. You can walk on it in socks the next morning. It only works if the existing finish is intact with no bare wood showing, and it costs $1.99 per sq ft.
